title: Spinal anesthesia
what: An anesthesiologist gives an injection in the lower back, putting medicine into the fluid around the nerves. The lower half of your body goes numb for a while, and you stay awake or doze.
why: For surgery below the waist: C-section, surgery on the legs, joints, hernia, or urinary organs.
duration: the injection takes a few minutes; numbness usually lasts 2 to 4 hours
tell_doctor: All your medicines, especially blood thinners. The doctor will tell you when to stop them
If you bruise easily or bleed for a long time
Inflammation or a rash on the skin of your lower back
If you have a fever or an infection now

prepare.title: Talking
prepare.text: The anesthesiologist will explain the method in advance and answer your questions. You can ask for light sleep during surgery.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Usually no food from the evening before, and no drinks for a few hours before. Your clinic will give you the exact times.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Do not stop them on your own. Tell your doctor what you take, and they will decide.

steps: An IV is put into a vein, and a drip is started
You sit and arch your back, chin to chest, or lie curled up on your side
The skin on your lower back is cleaned with antiseptic
First, the skin is numbed with a small injection
Then, with a thin needle, the medicine is given below the level of the spinal cord
You lie down. Within a few minutes your legs feel warm and numb
The doctor checks that you are numb enough, and surgery begins
feel: A small prick in the skin, then pressure in your back
Sometimes a zap down your leg. Tell the doctor, but do not move
Your legs feel warm and heavy, and you cannot move them
During surgery, you may feel touch and pressure, but not pain
after: Feeling comes back slowly over a few hours
The first time you get up, do it only with help from staff
Peeing is sometimes harder than usual. Tell the nurse
Sometimes there is a headache that is worse standing and better lying down. Tell your doctor. It can be treated
red_flags: Severe back pain, fever, or redness at the injection site
New weakness or numbness in the legs after the anesthesia has worn off
You cannot hold your urine or stool
A severe headache that does not go away: tell your doctor right away; after discharge, call emergency services

faq.q: Does the injection in the back hurt?
faq.a: Usually not. The skin is numbed first. You feel a quick prick and pressure.

faq.q: Can spinal anesthesia leave me paralyzed?
faq.a: Serious complications are very rare. The needle goes in below where the spinal cord ends.
No. A screen is put up in front of you. If you want, the anesthesiologist can give you medicine for light sleep.

reminders.text: Surgery under spinal anesthesia tomorrow. Eat and drink only until the times your clinic gave you. Bring your list of medicines.
